fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Decision-load risk at express-collector transfers during simultaneous signage/re-marking is a real human-factors concern, but the finding names no measured sight-distance deficiency, interchange specifics, or design speed, leaving it plausible yet under-quantified.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-CA-003 is referenced as defining a requirement but carries no quote or stated requirement text, and the core sight-distance claim rests on an unquantified scenario rather than cited measurements; only the detector-volume assumption traces to recorded input.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as a safety_concern with no compliance claim or fabricated normative basis note, keeping safety and compliance categories distinct under CRSAG semantics despite the planning-stage framing stretching toward implementation detail.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Phased one-interchange-per-quarter rollout with before/after speed-differential monitoring is specific, actionable, and verifiable, though it omits trigger thresholds or criteria for pausing further phases.
justifications.vru_coverage: Freeway mainline transfer sections carry negligible pedestrian/cyclist exposure and road_users is scoped to vehicle occupants, but the finding never explicitly acknowledges VRU non-applicability as the rubric expects.

justifications.substance: Resolving conflicting network-continuity records has real but indirect bearing on confirming the planning-stage scope boundary; it is process hygiene rather than a direct safety deficiency, hence marginal.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Only one context-use evidence id (EV-CA-006) with null quote is cited, which cannot substantiate the claimed conflict between two source records; grounded in recorded inputs but materially under-cited.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a compliance_question kept categorically distinct from safety concerns, and network-continuity scope verification fits CRSAG planning-stage semantics, though the normative_basis_note is null.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: names the responsible party (ministry planning office), the action (reconcile the two constraint records), and requires recording the outcome before finalisation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Corridor-wide network continuity at planning stage typically encompasses pedestrian and cycling route continuity, yet road_users is empty and no VRU impact or non-applicability is acknowledged.
